newsitem.title: USA: US agencies brief groups on school infrastructure.
newsitem.headline: US agencies brief groups on school infrastructure.

text.p: Federal officials are set to brief bond groups on Tuesday on the Clinton Administration's recent proposal to spend $5 billion over the next four years for school construction and renovation, a spokeswoman for the groups said Monday.

Catherine Spain, chief lobbyist for the Government Finance Association, said Tuesday's briefing by U.S. Treasury and U.S. Education Department officials was requested by the Public Finance Network, an alliance of municipal bond market trade groups.
Clinton on July 11 proposed that the federal government give localities $5 billion over four years to "jump start" school renovation and construction.
School districts usually raise school repair funds by selling tax-exempt bonds paying about six percent interest.

Under Clinton's plan, which faces an uphill battle for approval on Capitol Hill, the administration would subsidize construction loans by 50 percent, thus cutting a locality's bond interest rate in half to three percent, the administration said.
But Spain said bond groups need more information on the proposal.
"We'd like to know more," she said, including what bond groups and the White House will be "grappling with" when they take the plan to Capitol Hill, Spain added.

Clinton announced the plan after the General Accounting Office reported June 14 that many U.S. schools are in urgent need of repair. The report was commissioned by U.S. Sen. Carol Mosely-Braun, D-Ill.
